title: Maximum Subarray Sum With One Sign Flip
statement:
You are given an array `a` of `n` integers; values may be positive, negative or zero. You may change the sign of **at most one** element of the array (multiply it by `-1`), or leave the array unchanged.

After that choice, take a **non-empty contiguous subarray** and add up its elements. Print the largest sum you can achieve over all choices of the flipped element (or no flip) and the subarray.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `a[0], ..., a[n - 1]`.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the maximum possible subarray sum.

examples.explanation: Flip -5 into 5. The whole array becomes [2, 5, 3] with sum 10.
Every element is negative, and the subarray must be non-empty. Flip -7 into 7 and take just that element; flipping -4 or -2 would only give 4 or 2.
Flip -4 into 4 and take the subarray [3, 4, 5] with sum 12. Flipping -2 instead gives at most 1 + 2 + 3 - 4 + 5 = 7, and taking the whole array with -4 flipped gives 1 - 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 11.

hints: A flip outside the chosen subarray is useless, so you can assume the flipped element, if any, lies inside the subarray.
Kadane's algorithm tracks the best subarray ending at each index. Track a second value: the best subarray ending at this index in which one element has already been flipped.

For the second value at index i: either extend the flipped state (add a[i]), or flip a[i] now and attach it to the best unflipped subarray ending at i - 1 (or start fresh with 0). The answer is the best over all indices of both states.
